sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Setup, health check, and sign-up
sections.what: Sets the API address, creates a unique test account, checks the health endpoint, registers the user, and logs in to get a token.
sections.why: A unique account makes each run independent of the last.
sections.watch_out: Each run leaves a new account on staging.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Consents and upload address
sections.what: Grants the two AI consents, creates a small PNG, and requests an upload address.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the step names.
sections.watch_out: The consent and upload address results are not checked, so failures here still print PASSED.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Upload, confirm, poll, and chat checks
sections.what: Uploads the test file, confirms it, waits up to about 30 seconds for processing, asks the chat endpoint a question, then calls the data export.
sections.why: Covers the rest of the processing chain end to end.
sections.watch_out: The document ID fallback never runs, the polling loop treats failed results as finished, and the chat request uses a message field that may not match the contract.

summary: Script that runs ten checks against a live staging API, from the health check through sign-up, login, upload, processing, chat and data export.
purpose: Confirms that a deployed staging server works from start to finish.
why: Likely reason: a quick remote check after a deploy catches a broken release.
how: Each numbered stage calls one API endpoint with curl and reports pass or fail. A new test user is created and a tiny PNG is uploaded. The script polls for processing for up to about 30 seconds. The final banner says all stages passed.
inputs: An optional API address argument, which defaults to the staging address. Each run creates a test account with an example email.
outputs: A printed pass or fail for each stage, and a final banner.
risks: Several stages print PASSED without checking the response. The document ID fallback never runs, so a bad response can still pass. The test account is never deleted. The final line contains stray text that causes an error after success. The polling loop treats failed processing as finished.
debug: Run the stages one at a time, starting from the first failure printed. Check the API address and that staging is running. For stage 7, check the response contains a document ID.
